items.en: The $faction $fleetOrShip maneuvers to remain supported by the station, allowing your fleet to disengage. However, your forces are likely to be harried as they pull back.
The $faction $fleetOrShip maneuvers to prevent you from disengaging easily.
The $faction $fleetOrShip is attempting to disengage.
The $faction $fleetOrShip carefully maintains its distance, keeping ready to disengage in the event of hostilities.
The $faction $fleetOrShip assumes a neutral posture.
The $faction $fleetOrShip seems ready to fight despite being faced with superior forces, but isn't likely to press the issue.
The $enemyFactionAndTheirAllies maneuver to prevent you from disengaging easily.
The $enemyFactionAndTheirAllies are attempting to disengage.
The $enemyFactionAndTheirAllies carefully maintain their distance, keeping ready to disengage in the event of hostilities.
The $enemyFactionAndTheirAllies assume a neutral posture.
The $enemyFactionAndTheirAllies seem ready to fight despite being faced with superior forces, but aren't likely to press the issue.
It's aware of your identity due to your $playerFleetOrShip's transponder being turned on.
Indications are that it's aware of your identity, despite your $playerFleetOrShip's transponder being turned off, likely due to having seen you recently.
Despite your $playerFleetOrShip's transponder being turned off, it appears to be aware of your identity - likely due to the presence of notable ships in your fleet.
It does not appear to be certain of your identity. Any hostilities will have a reduced impact on your reputation.
They're aware of your identity due to your $playerFleetOrShip's transponder being turned on.

$yourForcesWereOrYourSideWas defeated in the last engagement.
$yourForcesWereOrYourSideWas utterly defeated in the last engagement.
$yourForcesWereOrYourSideWas victorious in the last engagement.
$yourForcesWereOrYourSideWas able to gain a complete victory in the last engagement.
All of your ships were destroyed in the last engagement.
There were significant friendly fire incidents over the course of the encounter.
Your forces engage in pursuit, as ordered.
The retreating enemy forces were able to disengage without losing any ships.
The retreating enemy forces were able to disengage, but not without taking losses.
No enemy ships managed to escape.
The enemy forces were able to turn the tables and hand your forces a defeat.
In a surprising turn of events, the retreating enemy forces were able to turn the tables and obtain a crushing victory.
$yourForcesWereOrYourSideWas able to disengage from the enemy.
None of your side's ships managed to escape.
$yourForcesWereOrYourSideWas able to turn the tables on the pursuing enemy and hand them a defeat.
$yourForcesWereOrYourSideWas able to turn the tables on the pursuing enemy and crushed them utterly.
The ships on both sides have been reduced to so much scrap metal.

But, not all is lost. You take command of the $boardableShipName, organizing repair teams and focusing on regaining basic propulsion and life support. Your efforts are successful, and several hours later, you're able to get underway.
The enemy forces harass your ships as they retreat, causing much disruption, but ultimately do not force a battle.
The enemy ships are unable to offer pursuit, allowing your forces to withdraw without further incident.
The enemy ships make no move to pursue, allowing your forces to withdraw without further incident.
The enemy fleet pursues your forces.
$yourForcesWereOrYourSideWas able to recover some combat readiness as they control the battlespace and the engagement was limited.
The enemy forces are able to recover some combat readiness as they control the battlespace and the engagement was limited.
Both sides are able to recover some combat readiness as they stand down after a limited and chaotic engagement.
The opposing fleet is able to disengage cleanly as your forces are unable to offer pursuit.
The opposing fleet is able to disengage cleanly as the forces on your side are unable to offer pursuit.
It looks like the opposing fleet will be able disengage without your being able to force a fight.
None of your ships are in any shape to offer pursuit.
Your ships are focused on regaining combat readiness and are unable to offer pursuit.
Despite retreating from the last engagement, your forces have disrupted the enemy, and can disengage without being pursued.
Despite being victorious in the last engagement, your forces have suffered sufficient losses to be unable to offer pursuit as the enemy disengages.
Despite being victorious in the last engagement, the forces on your side have suffered sufficient losses to be unable to offer pursuit as the enemy disengages.
After a tactical victory, your forces have an opportunity to cleanly disengage from the enemy.

Your fleet is too large to be able to disengage easily. Engaging the enemy and destroying, disabling, or forcing enough of their ships to retreat will allow your fleet to disengage without being pursued.

Your ships make no move to pursue, allowing the enemy forces to withdraw without further incident.
Your forces harass the enemy ships as they retreat, causing much disruption, but ultimately do not force a battle.
Your order a series of maneuvers that leave the enemy commander with progressively fewer and fewer options.
The opposing fleet tries to disengage, but they won't be able to get away without a fight.
The opposing fleet moves in to join battle.
Your forces pursue the enemy and manage to close in enough to force battle.
The $faction $fleetOrShip maneuvers for another engagement.
The $faction $fleetOrShip maneuvers to disengage.
The $enemyFactionAndTheirAllies maneuver for another engagement.
The $enemyFactionAndTheirAllies maneuver to disengage.
You cut the comm link and consider the tactical options available.
The salvage crews were able to restore basic systems on $repairedShipList.
Preliminary reports indicate $crewLost crew and $marinesLost marines were lost during the last engagement.
After the battle, $crewRecovered crew and $marinesRecovered marines were rescued from lifepods and intact compartments in the wrecks.
Your forces are preparing to begin salvage operations, when suddenly an enemy ship's systems come back online. A quick scan picks up $numLifeSigns lifesign(s) on board.
Your forces engage the enemy ship, and a few well-placed shots quickly neutralize it.

Your forces engage the enemy ship. A huge explosion blanks out the viewscreens shortly after a few shots impact its damaged hull, and all that's left when visuals come back online is a slowly expanding ball of debris.
Your forces move to engage the enemy ship, but its crew is able to bring the drive field back online at the last moment and it manages to get away.
Your forces stand down and let the enemy ship get away.
On receiving its orders, $boardingTaskForceShips moves in to approach the enemy ship.
On receiving their orders, $boardingTaskForceShips move in to approach the enemy ship.
A hard dock with the enemy hull is established and the assault teams quickly override the security systems on airlocks and blast temporary access points in weakened sections of the hull.

Assault teams are launched from about a kilometer out and approach the hull in waves, using personal propulsion systems to brake on the final approach. The defenders have an opportunity to fire on the landing forces with impunity until enough teams land to push inside the hull.
As your assault teams start to overcome resistance inside the enemy ship, it self-destructs. Most of the men and women in the boarding party are killed by the explosion.
The $boardingTaskForceShipName is destroyed.
The $boardingTaskForceShipName is seriously damaged.
The entire task force docked with the enemy ship is destroyed.
Some of the ships docked with the enemy ship when it exploded are destroyed, while the rest take serious damage.
Fortunately, none of the ships in the task force are destroyed.
After overcoming all organized resistance and sweeping every compartment, the commander of the boarding party reports the enemy ship secured and ready to accept a prize crew.

After overcoming all organized resistance and sweeping every compartment, the commander of the boarding party reports the enemy ship secured. Unfortunately, collateral damage from the fighting has crippled core ship systems beyond repair.
The entrenched enemy forces are able to hold back your assault teams long enough to finish engine repairs and get away.

At the last moment, the enemy ship regains propulsion and is able to alter its trajectory enough to avoid most of the incoming attackers, gaining enough time to get away. After a recovery effort, $boardingCrewLost crew and $boardingMarinesLost marine(s) remain unaccounted for.
You have no marines available to conduct boarding operations. Somewhat unhelpfully, an automated system chimes in with a projection that a boarding operation would have zero chance of success.
You have $marines marine(s) available. According to simulations run by a gamma-level AI, a boarding operation would have a $boardingSuccessChance chance of success.
An after-action assessment indicates $boardingMarinesLost marine(s) lost during the fighting.
The crew of one of your disabled ships has effected enough repairs for critical systems to come back online. If it's able to regain propulsion, it might be able to rejoin your fleet.
Unfortunately, enemy ships close in and fire a few well-placed shots to eliminate any chance of that.

Unfortunately, enemy ships close in and fire on it before further repairs could be completed. A stray shot must have collapsed the reactor containment field - the ship explodes, leaving behind a slowly expanding field of debris.
Before the enemy can close in, engine repairs are completed and the ship gets away to rejoin your fleet.
The enemy forces stand down and let the ship complete its repairs and limp away to rejoin your fleet.
You take command of the $boardableShipName, quickly organizing repair teams. If it's able to regain propulsion, you might be able to get away.
Before the enemy can close in, engine repairs are completed and you're able to get away!
The enemy forces stand down and let your ship complete repairs and limp away.
The last thing you remember is the sudden burst of acceleration as the escape pod you're in tears away from your doomed ship.
Salvage crews are able to recover $creditsLooted credit(s) from CPU cores still active in the wreckage.
You transfer command to $flagship for the upcoming engagement.
There's no salvage to be had.
Your $playerFleetOrShip does not participate in salvage operations due to its limited contributions throughout the encounter.
Your $playerFleetOrShip is able to participate in salvage operations due to its contributions throughout the encounter.

Your order $crashMothballList to power down all combat systems to avoid the risk of malfunctions during battle. The ship's crew directs all available resources to keep the engines running as smoothly as possible.
